programmes.t: Heal people. Lead in the hospital.
programmes.m: Few careers let you change a life before lunch. If you love Biology and Chemistry, you’re already speaking medicine’s language.

d.study: Years 1–2: anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. Years 3–6: hospital rotations in surgery, medicine, paediatrics and obstetrics, then a supervised internship before full registration.
d.entry: Usually A-Levels in Biology and Chemistry at top grades, plus a third subject (often Maths or Physics). Many universities add an interview or aptitude test.
d.cost: Among the most expensive programmes: tuition plus equipment and living costs. Look for loans, bursaries and scholarships.
d.dur: About 6 years, plus 1–2 years of internship.
d.where: A small number of university medical schools in most countries.
d.comp: Very high. Far more applicants than places, so strong grades and a backup plan matter.
d.day: Ward rounds, patient consultations, procedures and emergencies, then notes and teaching. Long hours and some night shifts.
d.sal: Among the best-paid professions in the long run, but junior doctors earn modestly while training.
d.suits: Caring, resilient, curious people who stay calm under pressure and enjoy lifelong learning.
d.alt: Nursing, clinical officer, pharmacy, medical laboratory science or biomedical science. You can often upgrade later or move into health leadership.

programmes.t: Turn physics into bridges, power and machines.
programmes.m: Engineers build the world everyone else lives in. Maths and Physics give you the tools; the degree gives you the blueprint.

d.study: Year 1: maths, physics and engineering basics. Later you specialise (civil, electrical, mechanical, chemical) with design projects, labs and an industrial attachment.
d.entry: Usually A-Levels in Mathematics and Physics at good grades. Further Maths or Chemistry can help.
d.cost: Mid to high; labs and project materials add cost. Industry sponsorships and bursaries exist.
d.dur: About 4–5 years including an industrial placement.
d.where: Universities and polytechnics. Check that the programme is accredited by the national engineering body.
d.comp: Moderate to high, depending on the institution and branch.
d.day: Design and calculations, site or lab visits, team meetings and solving practical problems within deadlines and budgets.
d.sal: Good and growing with experience, higher in specialised or international roles.
d.suits: People who like maths, building things and solving practical problems.
d.alt: Engineering technician diploma then bridge to the degree, technical college routes, or related fields such as surveying, computing or architectural technology.

programmes.t: Build the apps and AI everyone will use.
programmes.m: Every industry now runs on software. Learn to build it and you can work anywhere, even for yourself.

programmes.t: Care at the heart of every health system.
programmes.m: Nurses are the people patients remember. If you want meaningful work with real job security, this is a path with heart.
p: Room to specialise or study further

programmes.t: Be the person every business trusts with the numbers.
programmes.m: Every company needs someone who understands money. Master it and you’ll never be short of doors to open.
p: Can lead to CFO or own firm

d.study: Financial and management accounting, auditing, taxation, business law, economics and finance, plus data and software skills.
d.entry: Often A-Level Accounting, Mathematics, Economics or Business Studies at a solid grade. Good English helps.
d.cost: Moderate for the degree. Professional exams (ACCA, CIMA, chartered accountancy) cost extra and are often supported by employers.
d.dur: About 3–4 years, then 2–3 years of professional training.
d.where: Most universities and business schools, with many part-time and professional routes.
d.comp: Moderate. Many graduates, so good results and internships stand out.
d.day: Preparing and checking financial records, analysing budgets, audit work at client offices and advising managers.
d.sal: Stable and rising as you qualify; chartered qualifications raise it considerably.
d.suits: Organised, detail-minded people who like numbers and want a stable, in-demand career.
d.alt: Professional accounting certificates (ACCA, CIMA, AAT) studied directly, business or banking diplomas, or related degrees in economics or business.
